tldr: PairCoder is an LLM-based code generation framework inspired by pair programming, using a Navigator agent for high-level multi-plan exploration and a Driver agent for iterative code generation and refinement guided by execution feedback.
contributions: First adaptation of pair programming practices into LLM-based code generation with two collaborative agents: a Navigator for planning and a Driver for implementation
Integration of multi-plan exploration (Navigator generates and selects from diverse solution plans) and feedback-driven refinement (execution feedback guides plan switching or code repair)
Demonstrated superior accuracy over baselines: relative pass@1 improvements of 16.97%-162.43% on GPT-3.5-Turbo and 12.00%-128.76% on DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct 33B across five benchmarks
methods: PairCoder uses two collaborative LLM agents: a Navigator and a Driver. The Navigator first reflects on the problem description, then generates multiple diverse solution plans via nucleus sampling and selects k representative plans using text embeddings and k-means++. In each iteration, the Navigator selects the optimal plan (prioritizing correctness over efficiency), and the Driver generates or repairs code based on that plan. The Driver executes code on public test cases, producing feedback categorized as Pass, Runtime Error, Wrong Answer, or Time Limit Exceeded. If the Navigator detects that a plan has previously led to the same bugs (tracked in a historical memory module), it abandons the plan and switches to a new one; otherwise, it proposes a targeted repair strategy. This cycle continues until the code passes all public tests or a maximum iteration count is reached.
results: PairCoder achieves relative pass@1 improvements of 12.00%-162.43% compared to directly prompting LLMs. On GPT-3.5-Turbo, improvements range from 16.97%-162.43%; on DeepSeek-Coder-Instruct 33B, improvements range from 12.00%-128.76%. Evaluations were conducted on five code generation benchmarks using both open-source (DeepSeek-Coder) and closed-source (GPT-3.5-Turbo) LLMs. The motivating example from CodeContest shows that single-plan approaches get stuck in refinement loops on flawed plans, while multi-plan exploration enables finding correct solutions.
limitations: The approach relies on public (visible) test cases for feedback, while the final correctness is measured against hidden test cases that are not accessible during generation. The method requires a maximum iteration budget to control cost and efficiency, which may truncate promising refinement processes. The Navigator's plan selection and the Driver's code generation depend on the underlying LLM's reasoning capabilities, which vary across models. The paper notes that existing prompting approaches still struggle with complex programming problems due to rigid single-plan strategies, implying PairCoder may face challenges with extremely complex problems beyond its current evaluation scope.
